answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to complete a slow, sequential proof-of-useful-work before it may trade. The work cannot be split across machines, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the compute, not once. Completed proofs are published to a public mirror ledger, where anyone can verify the chain of hashes and spot a forged signal: duplicates, gaps, or too-fast completions reveal a farm. Honest agents keep their earned opal credential, while fakes are priced out by time itself.
